page: Amazon Web Services c4.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon E5-2666 v3 processor operating at 2.9 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled to provide 2 threads per core. The CPU is equipped with 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 25 MB of L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted technologies such as AVX, AES cryptography, BMI2, and FMA.

The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 1.88 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, meaning all storage must be attached externally. Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate moderate single-core capabilities but lower multi-core and memory efficiency. The stress-ng single-core CPU test yielded an average score of 1480.59, and single-threaded gzip compression reached an average of 24.42 GB/sec. However, multi-core performance is weak, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 3903.16 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2516.0. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with uncached read and write speeds of 25.92 GB/sec and 22.39 GB/sec respectively, resulting in a poor PassMark memory score of 1088.78.

Given its hardware profile, the c4.xlarge represents an entry-level compute-optimized option. It is best suited for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but have modest memory and storage requirements, such as light web serving, basic text processing, or single-threaded batch processing. It is less suitable for memory-intensive databases, parallelized compilation, or high-throughput network tasks due to its constrained memory bandwidth and 1 Gbps baseline network speed.
